decisive_items: involuntary movements of her left upper and lower limbs
Noncontrast CT of the head showed slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions without evidence of acute infarction.
Subsequent brain MRI demonstrated high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia.
response.rationale: Hemichorea-Hemiballismus is more specific due to the patient's symptoms of involuntary movements in one side of the body and imaging findings of increased density in the bilateral striatal regions and high-signal intensity in the basal ganglia

rejected.why: Diabetic Striatopathy is less specific and lacks direct evidence of striatal damage
Diabetic Chorea is less specific and lacks direct evidence of chorea
